lines.text: How far to the next place with a roof on it?
Further than you want to hear. Same as yesterday.
You've gone quiet.
I'm walking. It's difficult to do both properly.
Do you ever think about what you'd be doing, if none of this had come along?
Every day. It's mostly bread. I'd be making bread, and I'd be good at it.
...I'd come to that shop.
Something's been keeping pace with us since the ridge.
I know. Don't turn round. It stops being curious the moment we look interested.
{b}. If I go down out here, don't drag me home. Put me somewhere with a view.
You'd only complain about the view.
Then pick a good one and I'll have nothing to say.
I've stopped counting the days.
I stopped the week I met you. On the whole it's been an improvement.
You take the left side now without being asked. Did you notice you'd started doing that?
No.
Neither did I, for about a month.
You walked us straight past the turning.
I walked us past nothing. There was no turning. There was a tree you liked.
Must you breathe like that?
It's breathing. That is the entire range of options available to me.
If you've something to say to me, say it to my face.
I've been saying it to your back for three days. You haven't turned round once.
They're telling it in the villages now. "{deed}"
That's a better story than the one we were in. Leave it be.
{fallen} would have hated this stretch.
{fallen} hated every stretch. That was most of the charm of them.
Set the pace slower. You're favouring that side and you think nobody's watching.
...Slower, then.
You're bleeding.
It isn't mine.
Some of it is.
That went well.
That went quickly. They're not the same thing, and one day the difference is going to matter.
You put yourself between me and the second one.
You'd have done it.
I'd have thought about it first. That's the part I'm turning over.
You broke the line.
I broke the line because the line was about to have you killed in it.
Sit down before you fall down. I'll do the looking about.
I'm fine standing.
You are not, and I'd rather argue with you sitting.
First proper roof in a while.
Don't get used to it. I've got used to things before.
Tell the one about the ferryman again.
You've heard it.
I've heard your version. It gets a boat longer every time and I want to see where it ends.
...It was a barge, by the end. Sit down.
Somebody in the taproom was telling it wrong. "{deed}"
Did you correct them?
No. Their version had us braver in it.
You've taken the good side of the fire again.
I got here first. That's the whole of the system and it has served us well.
There's a place at this fire nobody's sitting in.
I noticed. I've been not-looking at it for an hour.
Say their name, then. {fallen}. It's easier the second time.
{fallen}. ...It isn't, but go on and I'll keep up.
We should say something.
We said it at the time. They heard the version that mattered.

reflections.text: You'll have heard by now — {deed}. That was us. I'm still deciding how I feel about it.
People keep telling the story back to us wrong. {deed}, they say, as if it were tidy. It wasn't.
Word runs faster than we walk. {deed}, and here we are, hearing about ourselves in a stranger's mouth.
{fallen} would have had something to say about all this. Probably something unhelpful, and probably right.
We buried {fallen} and kept walking. That's the part nobody puts in the songs — the walking after.
I still count us wrong. Every morning I count one too many, and then I remember {fallen}.
{friend} pulled me out of a fight I had no business being in. I've not found the words for it yet, so I'm using these ones.
Whatever happens here, {friend} and I have come through worse standing closer together.
That's {battles} fields we've walked off, and I remember the ground better than the reasons.
{battles} of them now. I used to be sick after. I'd rather have kept that, if I'm honest.
Somewhere behind us are {battles} fields where somebody's son didn't get up. I'd like this to be worth that.
Every floor of that tower we climb, the air gets older. I don't think it's meant to be breathed by us.
We are {floors} floors up a thing that was built to keep people out. Nobody has said yet what it was keeping in.
I could draw this country from memory now. Every ford, every bad hill. I'd rather have learnt it some other way.
We came in here bleeding and we're standing about making conversation. That's the trade, I suppose.
There are more of us than there were. I keep waiting to be told which one of us is the mistake.
We're carrying enough coin to buy a farm, and not one of us has said the word out loud.
{place}. Another one. They start to run together, and then one of them turns out to matter.
Say what you like about the road — it hasn't finished with us yet, and I've stopped expecting it to.
